requirements.title: Workflow-mechanics suites resolve in their own package roots
Consumers admit the evidence graph through one shared wrapper

properties.statement: Consumer suites load from the consumer root and shared suites load from the shared package in one report.
properties.oracle: A synthetic consumer package that provides the consumer suites and a real shared package that provides the shared suites; the report lists both selections and the failing group.

properties.statement: A consumer module that shares a shared suite's name cannot replace it.
scenarios: Consumer shadows a shared suite name
properties.oracle: The consumer fixture file fails when it is loaded directly, and the grouped run still passes.

properties.statement: Validation delegates to the shared graph and discovery ledger, and an unrecorded change without a graph is refused.
properties.oracle: The shared validator's own record for this repository's change; a temporary tree with an unrecorded change and no graph.

properties.statement: A recorded pre-adoption change reports a validation-only transition gap and cannot claim readiness.
properties.oracle: A temporary tree with a transition record and a change that has no graph.

properties.statement: Selectors reach the shared executor, and an unknown selector is refused rather than selecting nothing.
properties.oracle: The shared executor's requested-selector record and its invalid-selection rejection.

cases.setup: Write a synthetic consumer package with its own scripts/test_local_verify.py and scripts/test_openspec_workflow.py, then run the grouped workflow-tests entry with LOCAL_VERIFY_PROJECT_ROOT pointed at it.
cases.observable: The report lists the consumer selections from the synthetic package and the shared suite selections, and the run passes.
cases.red_expectation: A runner that resolved every name through one package root reports a load failure and returns non-zero.
cases.green_expectation: Both groups run and the combined report passes.

substitution.note: The synthetic consumer package is controlled input to the real runner.

cases.distinct_reason: Proves the consumer package supplies the consumer suites in the real two-group run.

cases.setup: Give the synthetic consumer a failing consumer suite and run the same grouped entry.
cases.observable: The run fails and the report names the consumer group.
cases.red_expectation: A runner that ignored consumer failures, or attributed them to the shared group, would not produce this report.
cases.green_expectation: The consumer group is named and the exit status is non-zero.

substitution.note: The failing suite is controlled input to the real runner.

cases.distinct_reason: Proves failures are attributed to the group that owns them.

cases.scenario: Consumer shadows a shared suite name
cases.setup: Add failing consumer files named scripts/test_requirement_tests.py and scripts/requirement_tests.py to the synthetic consumer, then run the grouped entry.
cases.observable: The run passes and the shared suite selection count matches the shared package.
cases.red_expectation: If the shared suite resolved through the consumer package, the failing shadow file would fail the run.
cases.green_expectation: The shadow files are not loaded and the shared suite runs from the shared package.

substitution.note: The shadowing files are controlled failing input.

cases.distinct_reason: Encodes the original collision report as a passing regression.

cases.scenario: Consumer shadows a shared suite name
cases.setup: Load the same synthetic shadow file directly with the consumer root as the working directory and module path.
cases.observable: The direct load fails, proving the trap is real.
cases.red_expectation: A shadow file that passed directly would make the positive case vacuous.
cases.green_expectation: The direct load fails with the fixture's message.

substitution.note: The direct load is controlled failing input.

cases.distinct_reason: Qualifies the trap so the shadowing regression cannot pass for the wrong reason.

cases.setup: Run the wrapper's validate operation against this repository's own change, which owns a graph and a discovery ledger.
cases.observable: The wrapper returns the shared validator's passing record and exits zero.
cases.red_expectation: A wrapper that reimplemented validation would diverge from the shared record.
cases.green_expectation: The shared validator's record is returned unchanged.
cases.distinct_reason: Binds the wrapper to the shared validator instead of a second implementation.

cases.setup: Create a temporary tree with a change directory, no graph, and a transition file that lists a different change, then validate.
cases.observable: The wrapper exits non-zero and reports `missing`.
cases.red_expectation: A wrapper that treated any missing graph as acceptable would exit zero.

substitution.note: The temporary tree is controlled input to the real wrapper.

cases.distinct_reason: Proves the admission policy cannot be bypassed by omission.

cases.setup: Create a temporary tree with a change directory, no graph, and a transition file that lists it, then validate.
cases.red_expectation: A wrapper that failed recorded pre-adoption changes would block adoption.
cases.green_expectation: The gap is reported and validation-only passes.

substitution.note: The temporary tree is controlled input to the real wrapper.

cases.distinct_reason: Keeps adoption possible for changes that predate the graph.

cases.setup: Run the ready operation against the same recorded graph-less change.
cases.observable: The wrapper exits non-zero with `transition_gap`, so readiness is refused.
cases.red_expectation: A wrapper that admitted readiness for a graph-less change would break the completion contract.
cases.green_expectation: Readiness is refused until the graph exists.

substitution.note: The temporary tree is controlled input to the real wrapper.

cases.distinct_reason: Separates the validation-only gap from a readiness claim.

cases.setup: Run the wrapper's query operation with --requirements R1 against this repository's change.
cases.observable: The shared executor's record shows the requested selector and exits zero.
cases.red_expectation: A wrapper that dropped selectors would query the whole graph instead.
cases.green_expectation: The requested selector reaches the shared executor.
cases.distinct_reason: Keeps affected-closure selection available to consumers.

cases.setup: Run the query operation with --properties R9.P9, which the graph does not define.
cases.observable: The shared executor's invalid record is returned and the wrapper exits non-zero.
cases.red_expectation: A wrapper that swallowed executor errors would report success for an empty selection.
cases.distinct_reason: Protects the zero-selection failure rule across the wrapper.
